sessionTitle: Build secure and enterprise-ready agents with Agent 365

announcements.name: Agent 365 control plane
announcements.shortDescription: A platform for discovering, governing, and securing agents across all platforms, built on Entra (identity), Defender (threat detection), Purview (data governance), and Intune (shadow AI detection).
announcements.longDescription: Agent 365 is positioned as the control plane for any agent an organization is building or running, spanning SaaS agents, endpoint agents, and cloud agents across different platforms and frameworks. It addresses the need to discover, manage, observe, identify, and govern agents, providing observability via inventory/registry, identity, threat protection against generative AI risks like prompt injection and intent breaking, data security against over-sharing or leaking, and governance and compliance. Kendra explains it delivers these capabilities not only for Microsoft agents but also for third-party, custom, and external agents, organized around three pillars beginning with 'observe' since you cannot govern what you cannot see.

announcements.name: Agent 365 SDK
announcements.shortDescription: A wrapper SDK (not an agent-building or hosting SDK) that makes external agents discoverable, assigns an agent ID, and enables observability, security policies, and the Tools gateway.
announcements.longDescription: The Agent 365 SDK is the mechanism for onboarding agents built outside of Microsoft. It is explicitly not an agent-building SDK and does not host the agent; instead it wraps an existing agent to make it discoverable within Agent 365. Through the SDK you can assign an agent ID, enable full observability, apply full security policies, and take advantage of productivity capabilities via the Tools gateway. Agent 365 is foundationally an end-to-end governance platform supported by trusted enterprise security solutions—Microsoft Entra for identity, Defender for risk assessment and real-time threat detection, Purview for data governance, and Microsoft Intune for shadow AI.

announcements.name: Registry Sync
announcements.shortDescription: Ingests agents from connected third-party platforms such as Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI into the registry for visibility, carrying over existing permissions like deletion.
announcements.longDescription: Registry Sync is a feature within connected agent platforms that ingests agents into the Agent 365 registry for visibility purposes. It takes your permissions and credentials across platforms such as Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI and brings those agents into the registry. Any governance capabilities or permissions you have across those platforms are also carried over and available inside Agent 365. This complements the SDK-based onboarding path used for custom agents built on frameworks like LangChain or AWS cloud solutions.

announcements.name: Agent 365 skills for coding agents
announcements.shortDescription: Roughly six (and growing) skills invokable from VS Code, GitHub Copilot, or Claude Code that instrument an agent for Agent 365 in about ten minutes.
announcements.longDescription: Agent 365 ships specific skills that coding agents can invoke to make an agent ready for Agent 365, demonstrated on a LangChain travel agent built on Node.js. The skills can be invoked from VS Code (via slash skills agent 365), GitHub Copilot, or Claude Code [inferred], and there are around six skills with more constantly being added. They include two 'make' skills plus piecemeal skills such as setup (getting an identity for your agent), instrumenting observability so the agent emits telemetry, and optionally adding Work IQ servers so the agent can interact with productivity surfaces. The process takes about ten minutes to run and ultimately makes the agent an employee in the organization with its own user identity.

announcements.name: Templates
announcements.shortDescription: A "hero" feature aggregating custom policies across Entra, Defender, Purview, and SharePoint into reusable templates applied during agent approval.
announcements.longDescription: Templates, described as one of Agent 365's hero features, aggregate custom policies from across Entra, Defender, Purview, and even SharePoint into one reusable template that can be applied to agents in a consistent and comprehensive way. Default templates are provided and custom ones can be created, including configuration of access packages, conditional access, and default policies such as DLP protection and lifecycle management protections. The template is then leveraged as part of the agent approval flow, where an IT admin team approves a published agent and applies the appropriate template.

announcements.name: Rules
announcements.shortDescription: Automation for lifecycle actions such as reassigning ownerless agents to a manager or auto-blocking agents when risk is identified.
announcements.longDescription: Rules inside Agent 365 provide a simple way to set up automation for lifecycle management actions across agents, replacing otherwise manual processes. Examples include agent reassignment—when an individual leaves an organization, agents built in Agent Builder can be automatically reassigned to their manager—and automatically blocking an agent when risk is identified rather than blocking it manually. The team noted heavy investment in risk to make this as scalable and easy as possible, with more functionality planned over the coming quarters.
